key_insight: A diffusion-pretrained language-model backbone plus multi-stage contrastive tuning yields multilingual dense and contextual embeddings that capture bidirectional, global passage context—enabling stronger retrieval from long documents with simple mean-pooling and late chunking.
problem_solved: Standard embedding pipelines and left-to-right pretraining lose bidirectional/global context in long documents, limiting retrieval quality and multilingual coverage at web scale.
method: Pretrain a language model with diffusion-based objectives to provide bidirectional attention and richer contextual representations.
Apply multi-stage contrastive learning at scale to produce two released embedding types (dense and contextual) optimized for retrieval.
Use mean pooling plus a late chunking strategy to preserve global context across long documents while remaining efficient for web-scale retrieval.
impact: Practitioners get embeddings that better encode bidirectional and long-range context for multilingual retrieval tasks, improving downstream search and ranking without complex chunk-level aggregation.
